source.title: Momentum Trading in Cryptocurrencies: A Comparative Study of Time-Series and Cross-Sectional Strategies
source.author: Adedeji Daniel Gbadebo

hypothesis: The paper's multi-horizon volatility-normalized EMA time-series momentum signal retains positive net risk-adjusted performance on eight major Binance perpetuals after realistic daily turnover costs.
data: Binance USD-M perpetual 1h OHLCV aggregated to complete UTC days; all eight assets required simultaneously after warmup.
secondary_smoothing: Use the long EMA horizon of each pair, consistent with the paper's stated 96+30+96 longest warmup.
bounded_response: u_k=tanh(alpha*z_k), equal-weight across the three horizons; composite is standardized by trailing 30-day std. Position weight is clip(S,-1,1)/N to enforce the paper's stated gross-exposure bound.
execution: Signal computed from close at t; applied to close-to-close return t to t+1. Daily turnover cost is charged when weights change.
development_gate: Canonical net Sharpe >0.80, canonical net total return >0, and at least 2/3 alpha variants have positive net total return.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0, positive total return at 2x cost, at least 2/3 alpha variants positive at base cost, 2024 and 2025 each non-negative, max drawdown <35%, one-day delayed signal remains positive, and removing the strongest asset contribution remains positive.
paper_deviation_notes: The paper reports gross results and does not include transaction costs, slippage, or funding; this test applies explicit turnover costs.
The paper does not specify the tanh sensitivity alpha in the accessible text, so alpha=1 is fixed as canonical with 0.5 and 2.0 as preregistered neighbors.
Funding is not available in the consolidated OHLCV panel and is not modeled.
